question: What is the primary reason governments get involved in the food supply?

options.A: To set the exact menu for every household
options.B: To protect public health and ensure stability
options.C: To control all farming businesses in the country
options.D: To eliminate the need for private grocery stores

explanation: Governments intervene primarily to safeguard the health and well-being of the population through safe and stable food systems. [learn more](GNS227_U2_T028#GNS227_U2_T028_h1)

question: How do poor food supply systems directly impact clinical nursing practice?

options.A: By forcing nurses to work directly as agricultural extension officers
options.B: By completely eliminating the need for hospital admission records
options.C: By reducing the total number of patients seeking emergency care
options.D: By increasing cases of malnutrition and diet-related illnesses

explanation: Inadequate food systems lead directly to health conditions like malnutrition and chronic diseases that nurses treat in clinical settings. [learn more](GNS227_U2_T028#GNS227_U2_T028_h1)

question: Which of the following is a core objective of government food intervention?

options.A: Ensuring food security for all citizens
options.D: Guaranteeing free food for international export

explanation: Food security is a primary objective, ensuring that everyone has access to safe and nutritious food. [learn more](GNS227_U2_T028#GNS227_U2_T028_h2)

question: Why is environmental sustainability included as a core goal of food policy?

options.A: To reduce the total volume of crops grown worldwide
options.B: To prevent farmers from ever using modern machinery
options.C: To ensure that agricultural land is turned into housing estates
options.D: To protect soil and water resources for future food production

explanation: Sustainability ensures that farming practices do not ruin the environment, allowing continuous food production over the long term. [learn more](GNS227_U2_T028#GNS227_U2_T028_h2)

question: What is the main purpose of agricultural subsidies provided by the government?

options.A: To lower production risks and support farmers
options.B: To replace natural rainfall with artificial irrigation everywhere
options.C: To increase the retail price of basic food items
options.D: To punish farmers who grow traditional local crops

explanation: Subsidies help farmers manage financial and environmental risks so they can keep producing food reliably. [learn more](GNS227_U2_T028#GNS227_U2_T028_h3)

question: How does government-funded agricultural research benefit the general public?

options.A: By ensuring that farming requires zero human labor input
options.B: By developing pest-resistant crops that secure the food supply
options.C: By removing all regulations on chemical pesticide usage
options.D: By discovering new ways to make processed foods last indefinitely

explanation: Research creates stronger, higher-yield crops that protect against harvest failures and maintain stable food availability. [learn more](GNS227_U2_T028#GNS227_U2_T028_h3)

question: What is the primary goal of government food safety regulations?

options.A: To increase the cost of importing foreign goods
options.B: To prevent foodborne illnesses and contamination
options.C: To make sure all food items taste identical
options.D: To prevent small vendors from selling fresh produce

explanation: Safety regulations protect consumers from harmful biological and chemical agents found in unsafe food. [learn more](GNS227_U2_T028#GNS227_U2_T028_h4)

question: A community experiences a sudden outbreak of severe diarrhea linked to contaminated street food. What is the most appropriate regulatory response?

options.A: Blame consumers for choosing to eat outside their homes
options.B: Wait for the outbreak to resolve itself without investigating the source
options.C: Inspect food handling practices and provide hygiene education to vendors
options.D: Ban the sale of all food items in the entire country permanently

explanation: Targeted inspections and education address the root cause of contamination while supporting safe local commerce. [learn more](GNS227_U2_T028#GNS227_U2_T028_h4)

question: What are national food buffer stocks primarily used for?

options.A: To dispose of old crops that failed safety inspections
options.B: To export surplus food for maximum international profit
options.C: To feed military personnel during peacetime training exercises
options.D: To stabilize market prices during shortages or surpluses

explanation: Buffer stocks allow governments to release or store food to control extreme price fluctuations. [learn more](GNS227_U2_T028#GNS227_U2_T028_h5)

question: Which of the following is a known risk of poorly managed government price controls?

options.A: Supermarkets will automatically lower prices on all luxury items
options.B: Agricultural land will turn into high-yield forest reserves
options.C: Farmers may stop growing crops if prices do not cover production costs
options.D: Consumers will completely stop purchasing staple foods

explanation: If price caps are set too low, farmers lose money and reduce future production, causing scarcity. [learn more](GNS227_U2_T028#GNS227_U2_T028_h5)

question: Which group is a primary target for specialized nutritional support programs?
explanation: Maternal and child health depends heavily on proper nutrition during critical developmental windows. [learn more](GNS227_U2_T028#GNS227_U2_T028_h6)

question: What is a major dual benefit of school feeding programs?

options.A: Reducing the operational costs of running public schools
options.B: Improving child nutrition and boosting school attendance
options.C: Training children to become professional commercial farmers
options.D: Eliminating the need for children to ever visit a doctor

explanation: School meals fight hunger while giving families an extra incentive to keep children in school. [learn more](GNS227_U2_T028#GNS227_U2_T028_h6)

question: What is the purpose of food security early warning systems?

options.A: To predict exact rainfall amounts for the next ten years
options.B: To stop international trade negotiations permanently
options.C: To warn citizens about high prices in luxury restaurants
options.D: To detect impending food shortages before famine strikes

explanation: Early warning systems monitor data so authorities can respond before a crisis becomes a full-scale famine. [learn more](GNS227_U2_T028#GNS227_U2_T028_h7)

question: A region suffers severe flooding that destroys local farms and displaces thousands of families. What should the immediate public health response include?

options.A: Waiting until the next harvest season to assess the damage
options.B: Distributing emergency food rations and clean water
options.C: Closing all local clinics to save administrative funds
options.D: Increasing taxes on imported relief supplies

explanation: Immediate survival needs after a disaster require rapid distribution of safe water and emergency food. [learn more](GNS227_U2_T028#GNS227_U2_T028_h7)

question: Why are nurses well-positioned to advocate for food policy changes?

options.A: They are primarily responsible for writing national agricultural laws
options.B: They witness the direct health impacts of poor nutrition in clinical practice
options.C: They control the financial budgets of international food agencies
options.D: They manage the commercial distribution of imported grain

explanation: Nurses see malnutrition and diet-related disease daily, giving them firsthand evidence of policy needs. [learn more](GNS227_U2_T028#GNS227_U2_T028_h8)

question: Which action represents effective nursing advocacy in food policy?

options.A: Personally financing the national agricultural subsidy budget
options.B: Sharing clinical data with policymakers to support nutritional programs
options.C: Refusing to care for patients who eat unhealthy processed foods
options.D: Replacing all government food inspectors with hospital nurses

explanation: Nurses use their clinical insights to influence decision-makers and support programs that improve community health. [learn more](GNS227_U2_T028#GNS227_U2_T028_h8)
